title: Narrative benchmarking
notes: We propose a P6 project comparing models through APIs. The central task is to recognize narrative categories in news paragraphs and provide inspectable supporting evidence. The implementation and protocol are prepared. Real empirical findings will follow once permitted data and API access are connected. Present this material as a research proposal and demonstration of software readiness.
source: Course kickoff, slides 7 and 9. Project proposal, 1 November 2026.
subtitle: API models, source evidence and resource trade-offs

title: Task boundaries
notes: We explicitly separate three tasks. The minimum project covers classification and source-evidence extraction. Discovering new categories requires separate human validation and different metrics. Finding a narrative does not establish that the news is false. A bounded task allows models to be compared on the same inputs.
source: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1513/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11128

title: An annotation example
body: Fictional target: “The column argues that the carbon tax raises bills without reducing emissions.”
Category: criticism of climate policies
Evidence: an exact source quotation plus a brief explanation
A paragraph may express several categories or none
notes: This is a fictional teaching example, not a real article or model result. Explain the distinction between the topic of climate policy and an interpretation portraying that policy as costly and ineffective. Multiple independent interpretations require multiple categories. A topical keyword alone does not automatically justify a label.
source: Author-created teaching example, data/demo/records.jsonl.

title: Literature and project decisions
notes: This is a synthesis rather than a claim to replicate all the listed studies. PolyNarrative supplies a useful operationalization. Other sources clarify the boundaries of metrics and transfer. Our study evaluates specific API configurations under declared conditions. Full citations and section-level reading guidance are in the literature review.
source: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1513/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11128 ; https://aclanthology.org/2026.eacl-long.176/ ; https://aclanthology.org/2023.emnlp-main.883/ ; https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1537/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09110
table: Paragraph labels and an explicit codebook

title: A focused research contribution
body: A controlled comparison of accessible API deployments
Classification quality and human-rated evidence support
Measured token usage, estimated price and observed latency
Independent validation on newly collected texts
notes: The contribution is a specific reproducible experiment. We do not promise a new architecture or claim that the field is unexplored. Useful findings may include limitations, unstable rankings or insufficient benefit from a more expensive model. Such conclusions must come from actual observations.
source: Proposed study design. Empirical findings pending.

title: Research questions
body: RQ1: How do fixed API configurations compare on narrative classification?
RQ2: What changes when we add fixed training examples?
RQ3: How well do frozen systems transfer to new texts?
notes: All three questions are measurable. For the second question, change only the inclusion of fixed training examples, keeping the codebook and output contract constant. For the third, do not tune on the new evaluation sample. The direction of the effect is unknown: few-shot examples can help or harm performance.
source: Project research protocol v0.1.

title: Experiment matrix
notes: Three models and two prompting variants produce six API configurations. The baseline is separate: its vocabulary and centroids come from train, and its threshold from dev. Exact models still depend on account access and supported interfaces. This table is an experiment plan rather than a completed comparison.
source: Proposed experiment matrix. No real API runs have been performed.

title: Dataset and split policy
body: Initial scope: English climate news and coarse categories
A verified PolyNarrative release, subject to approved access
Article-disjoint train, development and test data
A separate new corpus with independent annotation
notes: The package contains fictional demonstration records and a draft codebook only. Obtain and verify the actual release, including Other handling and split mapping. The validator detects article overlap and exact normalized duplicates, while semantic copies require additional inspection. Humans and models receive the same declared paragraph context.
source: https://nikon95.github.io/narrative-detection/ ; https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1513/

title: Execution pipeline
notes: Each stage leaves an auditable record. Evaluation gold labels do not enter the target request. Invalid outputs are retained rather than removed. Automatic evidence checking is limited to schema and exact source membership. The final review stage requires people and follows a predefined rubric.
source: Implementation: narrative_bench/data.py, prompts.py, engine.py, evaluate.py, annotations.py.

title: Classification evaluation
body: Primary: Macro-F1 over the fixed category inventory
Also: Micro-F1, per-label support and precision/recall
Valid-output coverage and end-to-end exact match
Exploratory uncertainty intervals resample whole articles
notes: Macro-F1 and Micro-F1 describe different aspects of performance. Disclose the treatment of absent categories and empty sets. Invalid and missing outputs remain in the evaluation denominator. They always count as failures for end-to-end exact match. Article-level bootstrap respects paragraph dependence, but separate intervals do not replace a paired significance test.
source: Implementation: narrative_bench/metrics.py and evaluate.py. Protocol sections 7 and 11.

title: Evidence evaluation
notes: A quotation can occur verbatim without supporting the predicted category. For example, the text may reject a position or quote another speaker. In the human audit, hide model and prompt variant, use a shared preselected record set, and retain unclear judgments. Evidence does not establish the model's internal decision mechanism.
source: Project annotation guide and evidence-review rubric.

title: Resource measurements
body: Observed input and output usage with a dated pricing snapshot
Median and p95 record latency, including retry time
Unknown costs remain unknown
Latency describes a model–provider deployment
notes: An API does not directly expose hardware utilization or energy consumption. Cost estimates use returned usage and recorded rates rather than prices taken from an old paper. Cached input is handled separately where data are available. A request-count cap is not a monetary ceiling. Set the monetary limit with the provider.
source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.09110 ; project research protocol section 6.

title: Independent new-set validation
body: Planning target: 150–250 paragraphs from about 30–50 articles
Two independent annotators before adjudication
A calibration sample excluded from final evaluation
Frozen prompts and models evaluated without new-set tuning
notes: The proposed sizes are planning targets to be refined after measuring annotation effort. Do not treat neighboring paragraphs as independent articles. Retain source URLs, dates, inclusion criteria and initial judgments. A new sample does not prove that texts were absent from model training without a verified cutoff.
source: Proposed new-data protocol. Collection and annotation pending.

title: Implemented research software
body: Python CLI with no third-party runtime dependencies
Chat Completions HTTP adapter and a CPU baseline
Immutable run fingerprints and a durable attempt ledger
HTML reports, error tables and annotation sheets
notes: Demonstrate validate, run, evaluate and baseline. The HTTP adapter has been tested against a local server, but account-specific compatibility still requires a smoke test. The baseline is TF-IDF nearest centroid. Raw PolyNarrative conversion is not automated: the package defines a normalized CSV/JSONL contract.
source: Source code in narrative_bench/. Test suite: tests/test_benchmark.py.

title: Offline demonstration
body: 35 fictional teaching records across train, dev, test and new
A fixed lexical fixture exercises the request and evaluation path
Reports include intentional keyword false positives
Demo scores are software checks only
notes: Open results/demo/test-zero/report.html and errors.csv. The science-museum example illustrates a keyword-matching failure. The demo provider ignores prompts and therefore returns identical zero/few predictions. This is not an LLM comparison. Neither these scores nor the synthetic new split fulfill the course's empirical requirements.
source: Synthetic data and fixtures authored for this project. No real news corpus or live API result.

title: Threats to validity
notes: No control eliminates its threat completely. Double annotation does not make a codebook universally true. Exact deduplication misses some syndicated copies. A provider may change a model behind an unchanged alias. Disclose these boundaries instead of treating a checklist as proof that risks are absent.
source: Project protocol. Dataset limitations: https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1513/.

title: Work plan
notes: The timeline follows the kickoff. The group assigns internal dates and owners. Divide data/codebook, execution and analysis/report responsibilities, while having at least two people annotate the new sample independently. By December, the objective is real preliminary results rather than only a functioning interface.
source: Course kickoff slides 7 and 9. Team-level dates remain to be assigned.

title: Final deliverables
body: A critical literature review and frozen research protocol
Reproducible code, configurations and run records
Real quality–resource results and evidence analysis
A newly annotated validation corpus and final report
notes: The final submission combines software and research reasoning. Document individual contributions. The kickoff weights are literature review 25%, implementation 35%, report 20% and presentations 20%. These describe course grading rather than the completion percentage of the current package.
source: Course kickoff slide 7. Proposed deliverables in project proposal.

title: Current status and next milestone
notes: Separate infrastructure readiness from a completed empirical study. The next practical milestone is corpus access and one verified development request for each selected API deployment, followed by a pilot budget. At present, no best model or achieved improvement can be claimed.
